Industry: Heavy highway construction and ready-mix concrete
Approximate Company Size Evidence: Company site states 750+ employees, 1000+ trucks and equipment, and 75+ years of operation. Iowa DOT bid tabulation shows a $12,391,845.42 Polk County award at the December 16, 2025 letting.
Signal Headline: Awarded $12.4 million Polk County paving contract at the December 16, 2025 Iowa DOT letting
Signal Explanation: Iowa DOT bid tabulations for the December 16, 2025 letting list Manatt's, Inc. as a bidding contractor on Polk County contract work with a project award amount of $12,391,845.42 for PCC pavement grade-and-new work. The company is family-owned and led by third-generation partners, and in 2025 it also opened a new 10,000-square-foot office in Ankeny.
Why Exit Factor: A $12.4 million Polk County paving award adds a large public project to a family-owned contractor that is also opening new office space, so this is a logical time to talk about capacity, management depth, systems, and enterprise value.
Evidence Excerpt: Letting Date: December 16, 2025. Primary County: POLK. Award context in the tabulation lists MANATT'S, INC. on Polk County PCC pavement grade-and-new work with Prj Awd Amt of $12,391,845.42.
Review Notes: Primary signal for this company. Co-owners named on the company timeline as the third-generation partnership include Adam Manatt and Greg Manatt; the 2014 transition text also named Tony Manatt. Brian Manatt is listed with Manatt's on the AGC of Iowa board (https://www.agcia.org/board-of-directors/). A separate 2025 Ankeny office opening is kept as an additional signal row and is not the primary record. Work-type text was taken from the tabulation extract; contract identifier in the extract was 25-77.

Approximate Company Size Evidence: Building the $148 million, 33-story, 390-unit 515 Walnut tower. Co-owner said daily site manpower is 150-200 workers. February 2025 interview said the firm had previously grown past 200 employees and later refocused on Iowa with a smaller direct team.
Signal Headline: 515 Walnut tower topped out in August 2026 on the way to a spring 2027 finish
Signal Explanation: On August 12, 2026, the Business Record reported that the top floor of the 515 Walnut tower was complete, roof components were being installed, and the tower crane was coming down. Andy Beal, identified in the article as co-owner of Beal Derkenne Construction, said 150 to 200 workers are on site daily and interior trades are stacked from the lower floors through level 30. Completion is paced for spring 2027.
Why Exit Factor: Delivering a $148 million high-rise with 150 to 200 people on site each day, while the co-owners are still directly involved in the work, is a logical time to talk about management depth, systems, and how much the company depends on its owners.
Source Title: Floor-by-floor: The latest on the 515 Walnut Tower project
Evidence Excerpt: With the top floor of the 515 Walnut Tower recently completed, work is continuing to finish the installation of major components on the roof before the tower crane is dismantled, said Andy Beal, co-owner of Beal Derkenne Construction.
Review Notes: Michael Derkenne is also a co-owner, confirmed in the February 7, 2025 Business Record interview. That interview also states the owners still do estimating, scheduling, and client meetings themselves. No public company website or direct phone was verified, so those fields are blank. Do not describe the owners as wanting to sell.

Approximate Company Size Evidence: Company site lists an Ankeny office at 301 NE Trilein Dr. and communities in Waukee and Ankeny, plus a Nebraska community. In a December 19, 2025 interview he said Sage put in about half the speculative houses originally intended for 2025.
Signal Headline: Owner cut 2025 speculative home starts to about half the original plan
Signal Explanation: On December 19, 2025, the Business Record quoted Chris Pickard, owner of Sage Homes and president of the Home Builders Association of Greater Des Moines. He said that in June 2025 it became apparent sales were not what Sage expected, so the company pulled back speculative construction for the rest of the year and put in about half of what it had originally intended.
Why Exit Factor: The owner personally cut the speculative building plan mid-year, so production decisions are still sitting with him. This is a logical time to talk about forecasting, systems, and how dependent the building schedule is on the owner.
Evidence Excerpt: Most of the builders I'm talking to seem to be cautiously optimistic that things are going to start to uptick next year, said Chris Pickard, owner of Sage Homes and president of the Home Builders Association of Greater Des Moines. I thought [Sage Homes] would build more spec houses this year but in June it became fairly apparent that sales weren't what we expected them to be, so we pulled back our activity for the rest of the year. I think we've put in half of what we originally intended.
Review Notes: Company phone and street address are on the Sage Homes site: (515) 410-9410 and 301 NE Trilein Dr, Ankeny, IA. A second Iowa number, (515) 523-4774, is listed for Kristy Leek on the sales team and is not stored as the owner phone. No owner email was printed. The June 2025 pullback is the event; the December 19, 2025 article date is the dated source.
